Order 
This Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed by the owner of the vehicle under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 26.11.2021 passed by the Member,
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Gwalior (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal")
in MACC No.929/2018, whereby the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation in favour of claimants (respondent Nos.1 to 4) and further held the appellant liable, along with the driver and the Insurance Company, to pay the compensation jointly and severally, with liberty to the Insurance Company to recover the same from the owner and driver.

2. Along with the appeal, the appellant has filed I.A. No. 3674 of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:10680 2 MA-4128-2025 2025, an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act read with Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking condonation of delay in filing the present appeal.

sentences.text: As per the office note, there is a delay of 1076 days in filing the appeal.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the learned Claims Tribunal passed the impugned Award without proper appreciation of law and erred in holding that the owner and driver M/S Samta Lok Sansthan Itm University ... vs Smt Shridevi on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144968800/

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the insurance policy nowhere stipulates that possession of a fitness certificate is an essential condition, therefore, the Claims Tribunal committed an error in holding that absence of fitness constitutes a breach of policy conditions.
Hence, it is prayed that the said finding be set aside.

4. To advance his arguments in support of condonation of delay, learned counsel for the appellant also contended that the impugned Award was pronounced on 26.11.2021, and the appeal was required to be filed on or before 24.02.2022.

Although the counsel before the Claims Tribunal informed the appellant about the impugned Award, he failed to disclose that the Claims Tribunal had granted liberty to the Insurance Company to recover the amount from owner and driver of vehicle upon finding breach of policy conditions.
The appellant came to know about this aspect only upon receiving notice in execution proceedings for appearance on 28.04.2025.
Thereafter, an application for a certified copy was filed on 23.04.2025, and the same was received on 26.04.2025.

Upon being so informed, the appellant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10680 3 MA-4128-2025 obtained the certified copy through its previous counsel, engaged a new counsel on 10.05.2025, and thereafter, the present appeal was prepared and filed on 13.05.2025.
It is thus contended that the delay of approximately 1076 days is liable to be condoned in the interest of justice.

5 . Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.6- Insurance Company opposed the application for condonation of delay and submitted that the delay of 1076 days is inordinate and has not been satisfactorily explained.
The plea of mistake on the part of earlier counsel is vague and does not constitute "sufficient cause" under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
It is further contended that appellant has failed to demonstrate due diligence and has not explained the delay on a day-to-day basis.
The law of limitation cannot be relaxed on such bald assertions, and condonation of delay would cause prejudice to opposite party, as the Award has already attained finality.
Hence, the application deserves to be dismissed.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

Upon consideration of the submissions and perusal of paragraphs 21 and 22 of the impugned Award, it is evident that at the time of alleged accident, the offending vehicle did not possess a valid fitness certificate.
It is well settled that a valid fitness certificate is mandatory for plying a transport vehicle on the road.
The legal position in this regard is no longer res integra.

A Five-Judge Bench of the High Court of Kerala in the matter of Pareed Pillai vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in 2019 ACJ 16 , has held that absence of a valid fitness certificate constitutes a fundamental breach.

entities.text: Pareed Pillai vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in 2019 ACJ 16
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Similarly, a Coordinate Bench of this Court in United India Insurance Co.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10680 4 MA-4128-2025 Ltd. vs. Vinod and Others ,
reported in 2020 ACJ 2641 , has held that possession of a valid fitness certificate is a statutory requirement and the liability of the Insurance Company is governed not only by the terms of the policy but also by the mandate of law.

sentences.text: Upon perusal of the impugned Award as well as record, it is not in dispute that the deceased was a ''third party''.
It is also undisputed that the offending vehicle did not have a valid and effective fitness certificate at the time of alleged accident.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation to the claimants, with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of offending vehicle.
In view of the above, this Court finds that the Claims Tribunal has rightly held the Insurance Company liable with recovery rights, and the same does not call for any interference by this Court.
9. So far as I.A. No.3674 of 2025, seeking condonation of delay is concerned
, the law on the subject is well- settled.

Although a liberal approach is generally adopted in matters arising under the Motor Vehicles Act, being a beneficial legislation, the expression "sufficient cause" cannot be interpreted in a manner that renders the law of limitation otiose.

10. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Esha Bhattacharjee v. Managing Committee of Raghunathpur Nafar Academy , (2013) 12 SCC 649 , has held that while adopting a liberal approach, the Court must ensure that lack of bona fides is not overlooked.

entities.text: Esha Bhattacharjee v. Managing Committee of Raghunathpur Nafar Academy , (2013) 12 SCC 649
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Similarly, in the case of Postmaster General v.
Living Media India Ltd., (2012) 3 SCC 563, it has been held by Hon'ble Apex Court that in the absence of a plausible and acceptable explanation, the delay cannot be condoned in a routine or mechanical manner.

entities.text:
Postmaster General v.
Living Media India Ltd., (2012) 3 SCC 563
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10680 5 MA-4128-2025 11.
In the present case, this Court finds that the delay of 1076 days has not been satisfactorily explained.
The explanation offered is general and vague and does not cover the entire period of delay in a cogent manner.
Mere attribution of lapse to the previous counsel, without any supporting material, cannot be accepted as sufficient cause.
The appellant has failed to demonstrate due diligence or bona fide conduct in pursuing the remedy within the prescribed limitation period.
Even considering the beneficial nature of the Motor Vehicles Act, the law of limitation cannot be completely disregarded.

12. In view of aforesaid discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that the appellant has failed to establish sufficient cause for condonation of the delay of 1076 days in filing the appeal.
Accordingly, I.A. No. 3674 of 2025 filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act seeking condonation of delay is hereby rejected.
13. As a consequence thereof, the present Miscellaneous Appeal fails and stands dismissed, being barred by limitation as well as on merits to the extent indicated herein-above.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
